short_description: The number of years the project is intended to be operational. This also sets the installation time of the simulated assets; once the project ends, these assets are considered 'sold' and the refund is credited against the initial investment cost.
The currency of the country where the project is implemented.
Accounts for the depreciation in the value of money over time. Commonly derived from the weighted average cost of capital (WACC).
Tax factor applied in the project's economic calculation.
Name of the country where the project is being deployed.
Latitude coordinate of the project's geographical location.
Longitude coordinate of the project's geographical location.
Name given to the project.
Name given to the scenario.
Brief description of the scenario being simulated.
Date and time when the simulation starts with the first time step. Also used for the result graphs and the timeseries upload.
Length of a simulation time step, in minutes. Currently only 60 minutes is supported.
Number of days for which the simulation is run.
Minimum share of energy supplied by renewable generation that the optimization needs to meet. Applies to the whole, sector-coupled energy system, not to specific sectors individually.
Maximum amount of total emissions allowed in the optimized energy system.
Minimum degree of autonomy that the optimization needs to meet. Applies to the whole, sector-coupled energy system, not to specific sectors individually.
Temperature of the high-temperature heat reservoir, at the heat pump's exit point. Temperature losses through the heat exchanger are not accounted for.
Temperature of the low-temperature heat reservoir, at the heat pump's entrance point. Temperature losses through the heat exchanger are not accounted for.
Measure of how efficiently the heat pump transfers heat from a lower to a higher temperature: the ratio of the actual efficiency achieved to the theoretical maximum (Carnot) efficiency.
Upload weather data file. Currently only TRY files are supported. If you use the TRY file from the German Weather Service, it should be a .dat file.
For fix tilt: azimuth angle of the module orientation in degrees (North is 0°, East is 90°); for tracker: azimuth angle of the rotation axis for tracking systems.
Tilt angle in degrees (0° is horizontal, 90° is vertical).
Performance ratio of the total PV system (usually around 0.8).
Ratio of the module area to the ground area of the module field, only needed for tracker.
Static system, east-west like system or 1-axis tracking system.
Reflection fraction of sunlight in the surrounding area.
Maximum tilt angle for tracking systems. This value is only used for 'tracker' systems.
Constant temperature or timeseries.
Select from one of the available BDEW heat profiles.
Total heat demand in the chosen time period.
Only for residential buildings, used for estimating insulation.
Windy for exposed buildings on free fields, near coast or high ground. Not windy for unexposed buildings in villages/cities.
